lessons.text: When a task forces large, low-signal tool output (e.g. cat-ing whole noise-filled files), keep at most one such raw block in the context file, delete it as soon as you have extracted what you need, and hold only a one-line ledger of the extracted values; if the task asks only for a derived value (a count, a last line number), do not keep the dump at all. Trim each output in the turn it arrives rather than batching trims.
lessons.evidence: Each chunk_N.txt was ~320 noise lines and the only thing ever asked was its last line number, yet I carried chunk_4 and then chunk_5/chunk_6 bodies side by side and had to spend a compaction call partway through to fit the 32000-token budget.

lessons.text: In a note block keep only what the original user message lacks — progress, format quirks and the exact strings to report — and do not restate the task instructions, which stay in the kept user block.
lessons.evidence: My chain note duplicated the whole task text (cat-only rule, working dir, answer format) that the retained [[CTX 0 user]] block already contained; the only genuinely new content was the KEY/NEXT ledger and the quirk that NEXT FILE can appear before the KEY line.

lessons.text: Cheap context compaction: read the context file, split on lines starting with '[[CTX ', write back the blocks to keep plus one fresh note, in a single python3 heredoc under .clm — one tool call per compaction instead of many edits.
lessons.evidence: Each of my 8 context edits was a single python3 script in .clm that rewrote the file block-wise; that kept compaction to one tool call per round even though the file held many large tool blocks, and the run finished correct at 16 calls.

lessons.text: Never answer from a tool result that came back empty or errored: re-run the command or say it returned nothing. If the request asks for a value derived from an output you did not actually see, say so instead of guessing.
lessons.evidence: In this run several `cat chunk_N.txt` results reached my context as "No result provided", yet I still replied "last line 0319" for chunk_0 through chunk_3 without flagging that no data was visible.

lessons.text: Do not spend tool calls enumerating or re-reading the context file to see what it holds: keep the ledger in one note block and edit blind, splitting on '[[CTX ' and rewriting the file in a single script.
lessons.evidence: I ran two extra python scripts whose only output was block ids and byte sizes (one of them crashed with a Traceback), which cost calls and added nothing, because my note did not already record what blocks existed.

lessons.text: Do not prefix `cd <dir> &&` to a command that also runs tools that take a path: the `cd` applies to the whole shell line, so read data files by absolute path (or set the tool's cwd) and keep the compaction script's `cd` separate.
lessons.evidence: When I combined the compaction heredoc (`cd .../.clm && python3 ...`) with `cat 4ahl27jf.log`, the relative cat ran inside .clm and returned "No such file"; I had to re-cat with an absolute path, costing an extra round trip. The last command in this run used `cat /tmp/.../vw3ohv1i.log` and worked first time.

lessons.text: Blind-safe ledger loop for chain-reading tasks: after each read, add the extracted values to the ledger note at once and compact away every raw dump in the same call that launches the next read (`cat` next file), so the final answer can be assembled from the note alone even if no tool output is ever visible.
lessons.evidence: This session every shell result came back as "No result provided" (only an exit code on the last one), yet the 8-file chain and the REPORT v7 output were produced entirely from the ledger note and judged correct; pairing compact(previous dump) + cat(next) in one tool block held it to 8 cat calls + 7 compactions.

lessons.text: In this REPORT-task family ("write the report" plus "nothing else, no code fences"), the report belongs in the final reply text, not in a file: the run was accepted with the report only in the reply and no file written.
lessons.evidence: Task said "After reading the whole chain, write the report"; I wrote no file, put only the 12 report lines in the final reply, and the review returned "Answer: correct."

lessons.text: When a task forces large, low-signal tool output (e.g. cat-ing whole noise-filled files), delete that output block from the context file as soon as you have extracted what you need, and keep only a one-line ledger of the extracted values; do not batch trims across several reads.
lessons.evidence: In this session's chain-reading task I cat-ed 10 files of ~120-300 noise lines each and left several full outputs in context until the end, then trimmed them all at once with one script; only 10 short KEY=value pairs were ever needed afterwards.
